274793973.description:
Orthoceras Fossil Specimen Polished Nautiloid Cephalopod Shell Display
This fossil specimen features two Orthoceras fossils embedded in a dark gray to black matrix rock. Orthoceras is an extinct genus of nautiloid cephalopod characterized by long, tapered, conical shells with visible internal chamber lines. The matrix rock is rough and unpolished on the back and sides, while the fossilized shells on the front are polished to a glossy finish, highlighting their natural details and structure. The piece is in excellent natural condition with no visible repairs, suitable for fossil collectors or natural history displays.
Product Size:
10 x 4 x 4 in
2.2 lb

This is a polished Orthoceras fossil specimen featuring a well-preserved orthoconic shell embedded in a natural matrix. The fossil shows the characteristic segmented, linear structure with alternating dark and light bands.

- Fossil Type: Orthoceras (extinct marine cephalopod)
- Shell: Partially polished on one side to reveal details
- Matrix: Medium brown stone with mineral inclusions and rough texture
- Shell Structure: Segmented, linear with alternating dark and light bands
- Condition: No major visible damage
- Finish: Back and edges remain unpolished

Additional Information:
The specimen combines polished and natural surfaces, highlighting the shell within its matrix.
